[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

No enterprise responsive layout pattern exists. Teams independently implement breakpoints, container widths, and grid systems, resulting in inconsistent behavior when micro-frontend modules are composed into shell applications across different viewport sizes. Healthcare applications must serve users on a range of devices — from mobile phones used by field staff to large-monitor workstations in clinical and administrative settings.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

This pattern establishes:

1. **Mobile-first breakpoint strategy** — Tailwind CSS breakpoint definitions aligned with the enterprise design system
2. **Container strategy** — Constrained and fluid container variants with consistent maximum widths
3. **Grid conventions** — 12-column grid built with CSS Grid; Flexbox for component-level alignment
4. **Responsive component patterns** — Stack → side-by-side → multi-column progression
5. **Touch target sizing** — WCAG 2.5.8 minimum 24×24px targets on mobile
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#when-to-use-this-guidance]

### When to Use This Guidance

- Building any page layout in a React application (shell or remote module)
- Implementing a form, table, or card-based UI that must adapt to multiple viewport sizes
- Designing a dashboard or portal with complex multi-panel layouts
- Ensuring healthcare portal pages work on mobile for field staff use
page_texts.7:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Consistent layout behavior across all micro-frontend modules in a Module Federation composition
- Mobile-first approach ensures core content is accessible on all devices before enhancement
- Enterprise breakpoints align with the design system token strategy (GUID-APP-UI-001)
- WCAG 2.5.8 touch target compliance achieved with documented minimum sizes

[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell healthcare applications serve diverse user populations: state agency staff on desktop workstations, clinical staff on tablets, and field case managers on mobile phones. Applications are delivered as Module Federation micro-frontends composed into shell portals. A module that renders correctly in isolation but breaks the shell layout on smaller viewports creates a poor user experience and increases support cost.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The enterprise UI stack (ADR-APP-003) uses Tailwind CSS, which provides a mobile-first utility class system. Tailwind's default breakpoints are used as the enterprise standard breakpoints, extended with custom container widths defined in the enterprise design token system (GUID-APP-UI-001).
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a standardized layout pattern:

- Remote modules use hard-coded pixel widths that break in shell application layouts
- Teams implement incompatible grid systems (some use Bootstrap, some use CSS Grid directly, some use Flexbox-only)
- Breakpoints differ across modules — a "large" screen in one module is a "medium" screen in another
- Touch targets on mobile are undersized, failing WCAG 2.5.8

page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#breakpoint-system]

### Breakpoint System

The enterprise breakpoint system uses Tailwind CSS default breakpoints, which are the single source of truth for all responsive layout decisions:

| Breakpoint | Prefix | Minimum Width | Target Device Context              |
| ---------- | ------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| (default)  | —      | 0px           | Mobile phones (portrait)           |
| Small      | `sm:`  | 640px         | Mobile phones (landscape) / tablets |
| Medium     | `md:`  | 768px         | Tablets                            |
| Large      | `lg:`  | 1024px        | Laptops / small desktops           |
| Extra-large| `xl:`  | 1280px        | Desktop workstations               |
| 2xl        | `2xl:` | 1536px        | Large / wide monitors              |

**Mobile-first rule**: Style for the smallest viewport first (no prefix), then progressively enhance at larger breakpoints.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#7-touch-target-sizing-wcag-258]

### 7. Touch Target Sizing (WCAG 2.5.8)

All interactive elements on mobile must meet the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum target size of 24×24px. The Tailwind minimum sizing approach:

```tsx
// ✅ Minimum touch target — inline buttons use min-w and min-h
<button
  type="button"
  className="inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center justify-center rounded-md px-4 py-2"
>
  {/* 44px is the Apple/Google recommended touch target (exceeds WCAG 2.5.8 minimum) */}
  Submit
</button>

// ✅ Icon-only buttons must have a visible or sr-only label AND adequate target size
<button
  type="button"
  aria-label="Delete record"
  className="inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center justify-center rounded-md"
>
  <TrashIcon className="h-5 w-5" aria-hidden="true" />
</button>
```

page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#review-checklist]

### Review Checklist

Before submitting layout code for review:

- [ ] Base styles applied without breakpoint prefix (mobile-first)
- [ ] Progressive enhancement added with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:` prefixes
- [ ] Container variant appropriate for content width requirements
- [ ] Grid uses `grid-cols-N` with `col-span-N` for column assignment (not manual pixel widths)
- [ ] Interactive elements meet 44×44px touch target on mobile
- [ ] Tables wrapped in a scrollable container on mobile
- [ ] `aria-label` on navigation regions
- [ ] Skip link present on page-level layouts (per GUID-APP-ACC-001)
- [ ] Layout tested on mobile (375px), tablet (768px), and desktop (1280px) viewports

[strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

1. Write styles mobile-first — no prefix means mobile; add `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:` to progressively enhance
2. Use the `Container` component with the appropriate variant (`default` / `narrow` / `wide` / `fluid`)
3. Page-level layout: 12-column CSS Grid; component-level alignment: Flexbox
4. Tables must be wrapped in a scrollable container on mobile
5. All interactive elements: minimum 44×44px touch target
